extracted.intended_audience: students and scholars of psychology, psychoanalysis, literary theory, and humor studies
extracted.subtask_description: Psychological and literary analysis of 'tendency-wit' (witticisms serving ends such as hostility or sexual exhibition), its social/psychic conditions, and the technical devices that make obscene or hostile material acceptable as wit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction: tendency-wit vs harmless wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency-wit is wit that serves a purpose (a tendency) rather than being 'harmless'; it gains access to sources of pleasure unavailable to harmless wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tendency determines additional pleasure beyond mere technical skill; when evaluating a witticism, determine whether it functions primarily to serve a hostile or obscene aim rather than only to display technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principal tendencies served by wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Wherever wit is not harmless it serves but two tendencies: it is either hostile wit (aggression, satire, defense) or obscene wit (sexual exhibition).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classify non-harmless witticisms by whether their underlying purpose is aggressive/derisive or sexual/exhibitory; the technical form (word- or thought-witticism) is independent of this classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition and dynamics of the smutty joke
rubrics_metrics.description: A 'smutty' joke intentionally brings sexual facts or relations into prominence through speech and is directed toward a person who excites the speaker sexually, producing excitation (or shame) in the listener.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether sexual content is instrumental (aimed at exciting a particular person/listener) rather than merely descriptive or scientific; note that a lecture on anatomy may be non-obscene despite sexual subject-matter if intent and social function differ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sexual element includes excrementitious/childhood domains
rubrics_metrics.description: The sexual element in obscene jokes often includes what causes shame and extends to the excrementitious domain—a holdover from childhood where sexual and excrementitious notions are undifferentiated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing obscene material, consider how infantilized or excrement-associated imagery contributes to its obscene charge and to the pleasure derived.

rubrics_metrics.name: Smutty joke as denudation/forced imagery
rubrics_metrics.description: The smutty joke functions like denudation of the person toward whom it is directed: obscene words force the attacked person (and listener) to picture sexual parts or acts and reveal the aggressor's imagination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether the joke's effect depends on forcing mental imagery on a target and whether that forced imagining is central to the joke's pleasure or impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conversion of sexual aggression into obscene wit under inhibition
rubrics_metrics.description: When sexual aggression toward its object is inhibited (e.g., by resistance), the sexual speech changes into obscene wit as an end in itself and often acquires hostile, sadistic features.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify situations of social or personal inhibition (e.g., unyieldingness of the woman, presence of a third person) that convert a potential sexual act into obscene verbal play; note the emergence of cruelty or derision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social conditions for smutty wit (presence of third person, resistance)
rubrics_metrics.description: The development of smutty wit typically requires the unyieldingness of the object and often the presence of a third person (listener/confederate); men may reserve smutty talk for times when a woman is not present or when resistance is indicated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess the social context: whether a target's resistance and a listener's role are present. Differences across social strata (e.g., rural/hostelry vs higher society) alter when obscene talk emerges.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-person structure of tendency-wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency-wit usually involves three persons: the wit-maker, the object of aggression/exhibition, and the third person (listener) in whom the purpose of producing pleasure is fulfilled; the maker often does not laugh—the listener does.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When judging a joke's effect, map these three roles and consider how the listener's reaction provides or legitimizes the pleasure the maker seeks.

rubrics_metrics.name: Absence of formal demands in smutty wit vs refined witty obscenity
rubrics_metrics.description: Common smutty wit often lacks the formal technical demands that characterize refined wit; conversely, in refined society, obscenity is tolerated only when made witty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish crude obscene jokes (where technique is poor but effect large) from refined obscene witticisms (which rely on technique like allusion); note that social acceptability depends on technical subtilty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allusion/substitution (representation through a trifle) as device for refined obscene wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Refined obscene wit uses allusion or substitution through a trifle—something remotely related that the listener reconstructs in imagination as a full obscenity; greater disproportion between offered and aroused content makes for finer witticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate use of indirect devices—e.g., understatement, metaphor, omission—to signal obscene content; the more the listener must reconstruct, the more socially acceptable (and 'witty') the obscenity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Function of wit: enabling gratification despite repression
rubrics_metrics.description: Wit allows gratification of cravings (lewd or hostile) despite hindrances (repression, social constraints) by eluding those hindrances and regaining inaccessible pleasure-sources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider wit's utility in bypassing internalized social/cultural prohibitions—wit functions not merely aesthetically but as a mechanism to restore renounced pleasures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Role of repression and culture in producing tendency-wit
rubrics_metrics.description: Cultural repression makes many primary pleasures unacceptable; tendency-wit furnishes a way to make renunciation 'retrogressive' and regain what has been lost under repression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When analyzing why certain witticisms resonate, examine the degree of cultural repression surrounding the subject matter and how the joke negotiates that repression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Indistinguishability of pleasure source (technique vs tendency)
rubrics_metrics.description: In tendency-wit we cannot clearly separate what part of the pleasure comes from formal technique and what part from the underlying tendency—'strictly speaking, we do not know what we are laughing about.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid attributing a joke's success solely to clever technique or solely to transgressive content; often both operate simultaneously and inseparably.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit as invective: belittling enemy to enlist third-person laughter
rubrics_metrics.description: Hostile wit permits us to make the enemy ridiculous through what cannot be uttered directly, thereby enlisting the third person (listener) and obtaining pleasure from their laughter.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess hostile witticisms by how they disparage a target indirectly and how they recruit audience complicity; note the ethical/political implications of using wit as a weapon.

rubrics_metrics.name: Wit for rebellion against authority and critique of institutions
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency-wit is especially adapted as a weapon against great, dignified, or protected targets—caricature and wit function as resistance against authority and as a socially permitted form of criticism.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Measure satirical or caricatural wit by its capacity to resist or undermine authority while avoiding the consequences of direct attack; the aesthetic value often hinges on this oppositional function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Façade formation and concealed tendency (comic or logical façade)
rubrics_metrics.description: Many witticisms employ a façade—comic or logical—that conceals a forbidden or critical thought; the façade dazzles or distracts the 'prying glance' while concealing the deeper tendency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detect hidden targets or subtexts behind superficially comic or logical structures; evaluate how successfully the façade masks critique and whether the masked content is what actually produces pleasure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sophistic/logical façade (displacement-wit)
rubrics_metrics.description: Some witticisms present a logical semblance (sophism) wherein the argument's chosen 'point' expresses an inner assent to a truth otherwise unsayable; such displacement-wit reveals the serious thought veiled by form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a joke appears as a 'clever' argument, look for the single concession or 'point' that betrays the speaker's real belief; classify such jokes as sophistic or cynical when they covertly assert unacceptable truths.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cynical wit as masked affirmation of forbidden desires/critique
rubrics_metrics.description: Cynical witticisms (e.g., 'Carpe diem' ethos, marriage-as-umbrella jokes) mask a frank criticism of morality or institutions and express truths about human desire under a veil of wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognize cynical wit by its underlying endorsement of pleasure or critique of moral precepts; evaluate how wit permits expressing socially taboo viewpoints about institutions (marriage, morality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Self-criticism through tendency-wit when directed at one’s own group
rubrics_metrics.description: Tendency-wit aimed at one's own composite personality (people, nation, group) functions as effective self-criticism because insiders can voice and laugh at their shortcomings with licensed authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Differentiate insider-generated jokes (which can be self-critical and subtle) from outsider jokes (which may be brutish); consider speaker allegiance when judging permissibility and authenticity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technique categories referenced (unification, representation by trifle, omission, absurdity, displacement, allusion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Witty technique includes devices such as unification (turning an allusion against an aggressor), representation through a trifle, omission, absurdity, displacement, and allusion—all used to veil forbidden content or to render it acceptable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In formal analysis, identify which specific technical devices are operative; stronger wit often combines several devices, while border-line cases may rely on only a façade without much technique.

rubrics_metrics.name: Border-line witticisms: weak technique but strong tendency
rubrics_metrics.description: Some jokes have poor technical workmanship yet produce strong laughter because their tendency (hostile or obscene impulse) supplies the pleasure; these are 'border-line' cases of wit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When rating a joke's 'wit,' separate technical merit from tendency-driven effect; acknowledge that a joke may be effective (eliciting laughter) despite low technical quality because of its tendency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audience persuasion via pleasure (prejudicing laughter in one's favor)
rubrics_metrics.description: The listener may be induced by the pleasure gained to take the speaker's side—even without full conviction—so wit 'prejudices the laughter' in favor of the speaker's opinion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess how laughter functions rhetorically to align audience sentiment with the speaker; consider whether audience laughter reflects persuaded belief or merely shared pleasure.
